claims.text: Transition-metal catalyst performance is governed by surface electronic structure, particularly the d-band center.
Alloying a transition metal with a second metal shifts the d-band center.
A shift in the d-band center changes the adsorption energies of reactive intermediates.
Raising the d-band center strengthens the binding of reaction intermediates.
Stronger binding of intermediates can increase reaction turnover and catalytic activity.
Stronger intermediate binding may promote side reactions and reduce selectivity.
An alloy catalyst with a higher d-band center should have a higher turnover frequency than the unalloyed catalyst under identical conditions.
An alloy catalyst with a higher d-band center may have lower selectivity than the unalloyed catalyst.
The hypothesis applies when the catalyst surface is the primary active site.
The hypothesis applies when the reaction involves adsorbed intermediates whose binding energies are sensitive to the d-band center.
The quantitative relationship between d-band-center shifts and activity or selectivity may vary with alloy composition and reaction conditions.
XPS or UPS can be used to determine d-band positions.
Temperature-programmed desorption can be used to assess adsorption energies of key intermediates.
